rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should establish a baseline for multimodal models. This tests the simplest multimodal configuration (singleprofile, pca_n2000 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, concat fusion) to evaluate if combining modalities improves performance. It isolates the effect of multimodal fusion and provides a reference for comparing more complex designs later.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat fusion) achieves 0.5266 validation accuracy. This experiment tests the effect of changing fusion from 'concat' to 'weighted' while keeping other parameters identical. It isolates the impact of fusion strategy, a critical design choice, and addresses uncertainty about whether weighted fusion improves performance. This is a logical extension of the current configuration and provides high information value with minimal changes.

Existing evidence shows multimodal models with singleprofile and pca_n2000+resnet50 achieve ~0.526 accuracy. This experiment tests the rna_only baseline with the same pca_n2000 encoder, isolating the impact of image data. It clarifies whether multimodal approaches provide meaningful benefits over RNA-only models, a critical design choice with no prior comparison in the history.

Existing evidence shows multimodal singleprofile models (config_016/017) outperform rna_only (config_001) with similar RNA encoders. This experiment tests multiprofile with the same RNA/image encoders but avgpool aggregation, isolating the effect of profile setting. It addresses uncertainty about multiprofile's impact while building on prior multimodal success.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with avgpool aggregation and pca_n2000/resnet50 encoders (config_018) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.6186). This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from concat to weighted (config_019) improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It directly builds on the strongest existing configuration while exploring a key design choice with minimal changes, balancing exploitation of current success with targeted exploration.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_019) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.639). This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l (a more powerful vision transformer) further improves performance, isolating the effect of the image encoder while keeping other components (aggregation, fusion) consistent. This addresses uncertainty about whether advanced vision models could outperform resnet50 in this task, leveraging the strong foundation of the current best setup.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_019) outperform others. This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more complex encoder) maintains or improves performance, isolating the impact of RNA representation. It balances exploration of key design choices while building on the promising multiprofile/weighted fusion foundation.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_031) achieve the highest accuracy (0.6776). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation (while keeping weighted fusion) further improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It is the best use of the next experiment as it builds on the strongest existing configuration and explores a critical design choice with minimal changes.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_033) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l (a more advanced model) further improves performance while keeping other components (scvi_n200 RNA, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) constant. This isolates the impact of the image encoder choice, a critical design decision, and leverages the strong prior evidence for transformer aggregation and weighted fusion.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_039) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder from scvi_n200 to scgpt (a more advanced model) further improves performance, isolating the impact of the RNA representation. It builds on the successful pattern of transformer aggregation and weighted fusion while exploring a critical design choice (RNA encoder) with potential for significant gains.
